label: Bending strength of an isometric member via the section modulus (R9)
statement_en: For a slender linear-elastic beam the maximum bending stress is the moment over the section modulus, σ_b = F ℓ / Z. With similar sections (Z ∝ L^3) and a lever arm ∝ L: if the load scales as the body (F ∝ L^3, R9a) then σ_b scales as L, the bending safety factor σ_max/σ_b equals σ_max k_Z/(k_F k_ℓ L) and above L_max,b = σ_max k_Z/(k_F k_ℓ n) the member cannot carry n times its load; if the load scales as an area (a lamina of constant thickness, F ∝ L^2, R9b) then σ_b is independent of size and no size limit follows.

hypotheses.name: scaling-bending-law#assumed-1
hypotheses.statement: Slender linear-elastic (Euler-Bernoulli) beam; σ_b = M_b/Z with a point load at the free end (a distributed load changes the constant, not the L-dependence).

hypotheses.name: scaling-bending-law#assumed-2
hypotheses.statement: Geometrically similar sections (Z = k_Z d^3, d ∝ L) and lever arm ∝ L; elastic similarity (d ∝ ℓ^(3/2)) is a different hypothesis family, not formalised.

hypotheses.name: scaling-bending-law#assumed-3
hypotheses.statement: Constant σ_max; static loads only (wind on a leaf is outside the model); which load family applies (R9a or R9b) is empirical and must be committed by the candidate.

scope.basis: a theorem about a model: it applies wherever the design supplies the quantities it uses and accepts the hypotheses in scope.assumed
kernelChecked: R9a: with CubeLaw F, LeverLaw ℓ and SectionModulusLaw Z, σ_b(L2)/σ_b(L1) = L2/L1, log exponent 1 (bendingStress_ratio_body, bendingStress_log_body); σ_max/σ_b = σ_max k_Z/(k_F k_ℓ L) (bendingSafety_eq); above σ_max k_Z/(k_F k_ℓ n) the stress at n times the load exceeds σ_max (bending_cannot_carry).
R9b: with AreaLaw F instead, σ_b(L2)/σ_b(L1) = 1, log exponent 0 (bendingStress_ratio_sheet, bendingStress_log_sheet): no size limit follows.

lean.source:
/-- **R9a, conclusion 1 (body-like load).** With the load scaling as the body (`CubeLaw F`), lever arm `∝ L` and
similar sections (`Z ∝ L³`), bending stress scales as `L`. -/
theorem bendingStress_ratio_body {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ : ℝ} (hF : CubeLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) :
    bendingStress F ℓ Z L₂ / bendingStress F ℓ Z L₁ = L₂ / L₁ := by
  unfold bendingStress
  rw [hF.2 L₁ h₁, hF.2 L₂ h₂, hℓ.2 L₁ h₁, hℓ.2 L₂ h₂, hZ.2 L₁ h₁, hZ.2 L₂ h₂]
  have := hF.1; have := hℓ.1; have := hZ.1
  field_simp

named_hypotheses.name: Delphi.SectionModulusLaw
named_hypotheses.source:
/-- Geometrically similar sections: the section modulus is `k L³` (`Z = k_Z d³` with `d = k_d L`). -/
def SectionModulusLaw (Z : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℝ) : Prop := 0 < k ∧ ∀ L, 0 < L → Z L = k * L ^ 3

named_hypotheses.name: Delphi.LeverLaw
named_hypotheses.source:
/-- The lever arm scales with the body: `ℓ = k L`. -/
def LeverLaw (ℓ : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℝ) : Prop := 0 < k ∧ ∀ L, 0 < L → ℓ L = k * L

constraint_details.relation: d log σ_b / d log L = 1
constraint_details.canEliminate: a candidate asserting a body-like load and similar sections with a bending-stress exponent other than 1; an exponent of 1 is the theorem and is consistent (WP-077/C1)
constraint_details.lemma_source:
/-- **C12, bending exponent, body-like load.** Under R9a the exponent of bending stress on `L` is `1`. -/
theorem bending_exponent_rules_out {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ : ℝ} (hF : CubeLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L₁ L₂ b : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) (hne : L₁ ≠ L₂)
    (hb : Real.log (bendingStress F ℓ Z L₂ / bendingStress F ℓ Z L₁) = b * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)) (h : b ≠ 1) :
    False := by
  have := bendingStress_log_body hF hℓ hZ h₁ h₂
  rw [hb] at this
  exact h (mul_right_cancel₀ (log_ratio_ne_zero h₁ h₂ hne) this)

constraint_details.canEliminate: a candidate committing a bending-stress ratio other than its length ratio under R9a
constraint_details.lemma_source:
/-- **C12b, bending ratio, body-like load.** A committed bending-stress ratio `r ≠ ℓ` is ruled out. -/
theorem bending_ratio_rules_out {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ : ℝ} (hF : CubeLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L₁ L₂ r q : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂)
    (hr : bendingStress F ℓ Z L₂ / bendingStress F ℓ Z L₁ = r) (hq : L₂ / L₁ = q) (hne : r ≠ q) : False := by
  have := bendingStress_ratio_body hF hℓ hZ h₁ h₂
  rw [hr, hq] at this
  exact hne this

constraint_details.relation: d log σ_b / d log L = 0
constraint_details.canEliminate: a candidate that commits to a constant-thickness blade and still claims bending stress rises with size (hence a bending size limit); under R9b no limit follows
constraint_details.lemma_source:
/-- **C12c, bending exponent, sheet-like load.** Under R9b the exponent is `0`: a candidate with a constant-thickness
lamina that still commits to bending stress rising (or falling) with size is ruled out. -/
theorem bending_exponent_sheet_rules_out {F ℓ Z : ℝ → ℝ} {kF kℓ kZ : ℝ} (hF : AreaLaw F kF) (hℓ : LeverLaw ℓ kℓ)
    (hZ : SectionModulusLaw Z kZ) {L₁ L₂ b : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) (hne : L₁ ≠ L₂)
    (hb : Real.log (bendingStress F ℓ Z L₂ / bendingStress F ℓ Z L₁) = b * Real.log (L₂ / L₁)) (h : b ≠ 0) :
    False := by
  have := bendingStress_log_sheet hF hℓ hZ h₁ h₂
  rw [hb] at this
  exact h (mul_right_cancel₀ (log_ratio_ne_zero h₁ h₂ hne) this)
